column4: Visit note | 2026-07-19 04:30 PM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Tasnim Siddique, 41, female. Mrs. Siddique states that she experiences a burning sensation when passing urine, along with a dull lower belly ache and the need to go to the toilet much more often. She is a CNG auto-rickshaw driver and mentions that her discomfort started after a long trip to Bashundhara. She has a history of Bronchial asthma. She denies any fever, chills, or back pain. On examination: temperature 99.0 F, BP 119/74 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 85 kg. Chest is clear and abdomen is soft with mild suprapubic tenderness. Assessment: Uncomplicated urinary tract infection. Plan: a prescription was issued for her treatment. She was advised to drink at least two litres of water daily and not to hold urine for long. Follow-up in 1 week if symptoms continue.
